chunks: Concerning two men who testified against a man that he stole, so his hand was cut, then one of them retracted and said, “I was mistaken about this one, but it was someone else”: half of the blood-money of the hand is due from him, and his testimony regarding the other person is not accepted. If both retract together and say, “We were mistaken; rather, the thief was so-and-so,” then the blood-money of the hand is due from them, and their testimony regarding the other person is not accepted. If they say, “We did it deliberately,” the hand of one of them is cut in return for the hand of the one whose hand was cut, and the one whose hand is not cut pays back one quarter of the full blood-money of a man to the guardians of the man whose hand was cut. If the first amputee says, “I do not consent unless both of their hands are cut together,” then he returns the blood-money of one hand, to be divided between them, and both of their hands are cut.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ: the legal guardians or entitled heirs
key_terms.دِيَةِ الْيَدِ: the financial compensation for a severed hand
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُ: his legal testimony as a witness
key_terms.فَقُطِعَ: his hand was amputated as legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if witnesses retract testimony after a theft punishment has already been carried out?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for false testimony in a theft case that resulted in amputation. It distinguishes between mistaken testimony and deliberate false testimony, assigning financial liability in the first case and retaliatory punishment in the second, while also invalidating later testimony against another accused person.
